context: Product topology on arbitrary indexed Cartesian product, two equivalent subbasis and finite-support basis descriptions / projection-cylinder-subbasis
editorial_note: The directly read ProofWiki Product Topology page defines the smallest topology making coordinate projections continuous by the SUBBASIS of cylinder preimages π_i^{-1}(U). Its Also See directly states the finite-coordinate-support natural basis; the linked Natural Basis of Product Topology theorem was independently read, and shows equivalence by finite intersections of cylinder sets. Both are equivalent formulations of ONE indexed-product topology, not different meanings. IMPORTANT: the set of individual cylinder preimages is a subbasis, generally NOT the complete topology or a basis closed under finite intersections. The product topology of infinitely many factors is not generally the BOX topology whose product basic open sets may restrict infinitely many coordinates. An empty index set produces a singleton product with unique topology. Empty factor spaces produce an empty product; this definition does not require nonempty factors. Product topology T^D on function space is the special case X_i=T for each index i∈D; this supplies the previously missing pointwise-convergence prerequisite. No Hausdorff, compactness, metric or continuity of maps into X is silently imposed. Sections: General definition by generated inverse-image subbasis, Natural basis using finite coordinate restrictions linked to separate directly inspected theorem https://proofwiki.org/wiki/Natural_Basis_of_Product_Topology, Finite product is specialization
text: Let {(X_i,τ_i)}_{i∈I} be topological spaces and X=∏_{i∈I}X_i, with projection π_i:X→X_i. The product topology on X is the topology generated by the subbasis {π_i⁻¹(U):i∈I,U∈τ_i}.

context: Eigenvalue scalar for a K-linear endomorphism V→V, two equivalent nonzero-vector tests / nontrivial-shifted-kernel
editorial_note: ProofWiki's Eigenvalue page directly defines operator eigenvalue λ as ker(A−λI) distinct from the singleton {0_V}; the second equivalent nonzero-vector test follows immediately from the definition of kernel and is independently supported on the same source page by its Real Square Matrix specialization. The eigenvalue is the SCALAR λ, not a nonzero eigenvector or eigenspace. A must be K-linear V→V, not an arbitrary map V→W, because λI_V must share domain and codomain with A. For the zero-dimensional vector space, there are no eigenvalues (all shifted kernels equal {0}). No finite-dimensionality assumed for V in the operator case; do not impose determinant, characteristic-polynomial or matrix formulations from finite square matrices. The source also defines eigenvalues of matrices over a commutative ring and eigenfunctions: those are separately scoped, not automatically equivalent to this operator meaning. Avoid circular prerequisites: eigenvalue should depend directly on linear map and kernel, not on the earlier eigenvector meaning that presupposes an eigenvalue. Sections: Linear Operator kernel nontrivial definition, Real Square Matrix specialized existence criterion, Distinct commutative-ring square-matrix and eigenfunction contexts excluded
text: For a K-vector space V and K-linear operator A:V→V, λ∈K is an eigenvalue of A if ker(A−λI_V)≠{0_V}, where I_V is the identity map of V.

context: Nonempty simple undirected graph with paths between every vertex pair / all-vertex-pairs-joined-by-walk
editorial_note: The directly read ProofWiki Connected (Graph Theory)/Graph definition says a graph is connected exactly when every pair of vertices is connected; its linked Vertices page was separately inspected and says equal vertices are connected, while distinct vertices require a walk. This screen specializes to a nonempty SIMPLE UNDIRECTED graph, providing an unambiguous convention about empty graphs. The source's all-pairs condition alone is vacuous for empty V, while some textbooks require at least one vertex; requiring nonempty V explicitly avoids silently treating empty graphs as connected and honestly records that convention as an editorial scope restriction. A walk can repeat vertices; in a simple undirected graph, a walk between two vertices exists iff a simple path exists, so path-based and walk-based presentations are equivalent but only one source form is admitted here. No finiteness of V is assumed; only individual connecting walks must be finite. Connectedness is about vertex pairs and is not the same as graph completeness (an edge between every distinct pair). Sections: Graph connected when every pair of vertices connected, Vertex-pair connectivity source https://proofwiki.org/wiki/Definition:Connected_(Graph_Theory)/Vertices read separately, Disconnected as negation
text: A nonempty simple undirected graph G=(V,E) is connected if for all u,v∈V there exists a finite walk from u to v, allowing the length-zero walk when u=v.

context: Convergent real-valued exponential generating function on its real convergence set / factorial-denominator-convergent-egf
editorial_note: The directly inspected ProofWiki Exponential Generating Function page defines G_A(z)=Σ_{n≥0} a_n z^n/n! for a REAL sequence and explicitly restricts the function domain to arguments where the series converges. This approved meaning specializes its z variable to real values and does not claim complex analyticity without sources. It is NOT the ordinary generating function Σa_n z^n of the SAME sequence unless specific coefficient conditions happen to make them coincide. It can be described as an ordinary generating function of a transformed sequence b_n=a_n/n!, but that transformation is a mathematical relation and not a claim that the two generators are synonymous under original coefficients. A formal EGF may be defined without convergence in a separate algebraic context; it is NOT this real-function meaning. Its n! denominator is mathematically essential, and the source's optional starting index b>0 with earlier zero coefficients is merely a special convention. No positivity, probability normalization, radius of convergence or arbitrary all-real evaluation is assumed. Sections: Definition with a_n z^n/n!, Explicit convergence-domain restriction, Starting sum index b treated as special reindexing
text: For a real sequence (a_n)_{n≥0}, let D={z∈ℝ:∑_{n=0}^∞(a_n/n!)z^n converges}. Its exponential generating function E_A:D→ℝ is E_A(z)=∑_{n=0}^∞(a_n/n!)z^n.
